objectives.understand: Why a decisions-relevant summary beats 'summarise this', and where AI calculations can go wrong.
objectives.do: Run the decisions-summary prompt and describe a spreadsheet so AI writes the formulas.
objectives.demonstrate: Pick the right summary questions, check a formula and a total, and know what revenue does not tell you.
objectives.apply: Produce one verified summary of a real document and one working spreadsheet.

discover.title: Mission briefing: 40 pages before Monday
discover.scenario: Friday 5pm. Your director forwards a 40-page donor policy with one line: 'What does this mean for us? Meeting Monday 9am.' Meanwhile your sales notebook for the shop is two months behind. Today you answer the director in minutes, quote by quote, and get a spreadsheet that does the maths, which you then check.

keyIdeas: Ask what the document requires you to do, by when, at what cost, and what decisions are needed. Quote the section for each.
Describe the columns and calculations; the AI writes the formulas and explains each one.
Check every total yourself. Revenue is not profit.

missions.title: Ask the right questions of the document
missions.scenario: Your director needs to act on the 40-page donor policy on Monday.
missions.prompt: Which instructions belong in your decisions-summary prompt? Select all that apply.

options.text: What does this require ME to do, and by when?
options.feedback: Yes. Actions and deadlines are what your director needs.
Yes. Cost drives most decisions above you.

options.text: Quote the exact section for each answer, and say 'not stated' if the document doesn't answer.
options.feedback: Yes. Quotes let you check, and 'not stated' stops guessing.

options.text: Make it sound impressive for the director.
options.feedback: No. Style isn't the problem; decisions and evidence are.

options.text: Fill in anything missing with what such policies usually say.
options.feedback: No. That invites invention. Missing answers should come back as 'not stated'.

missions.hint: The director needs actions, deadlines, costs and decisions, all traceable to the document.
missions.support: Imagine the director asks 'where does it say that?' Your prompt must make the AI answer the practical questions and point to the exact section, without guessing.
missions.explain: The decisions-relevant summary asks what, by when, at what cost and what decisions, with quotes. 'Not stated' is a valid and valuable answer, so the AI doesn't fill gaps.

missions.title: Check the AI's spreadsheet
missions.scenario: You described a sales sheet. The AI returned: row 2, Notebooks, Quantity 2, Unit price 1500, Total =B2*C2; row 3, Pens, Quantity 3, Unit price 200, Total =B3*C3; Grand total =SUM(D2:D4).
missions.prompt: What should you do before you rely on it?

options.text: Nothing. AI is good at maths, and the formulas look right.
options.feedback: Formulas can look right and still be wrong. Today's rule is to check every total yourself.

options.text: Notice the grand total covers D2:D4 when the data is in D2:D3, then check by hand: 2 × 1,500 + 3 × 200 = ₦3,600.
options.feedback: Yes. The range includes an extra row that could pick up a stray value later, and the hand check confirms ₦3,600.
That is revenue, not profit. Stock costs and expenses aren't included.

options.text: Delete the formulas and type the totals in by hand.
options.feedback: That throws away the benefit of the spreadsheet. Fix the range and keep the formulas.

missions.hint: Read the cell ranges closely, and do the maths yourself.
missions.support: The data sits in rows 2 and 3. Look at which rows the SUM formula covers. Then multiply each quantity by its price and add them on a calculator.
missions.explain: Small formula slips like an extra row in a range are common. A one-minute hand check (2 × 1,500 + 3 × 200 = 3,600) catches them, and remember the total is sales revenue, not profit.

advanced.title: Advanced: summarise a document too long to paste
advanced.scenario: A 90-page procurement guideline is too long for one paste on the free tier.
advanced.prompt: Order the steps for summarising it reliably.
items: Paste the decisions-summary prompt with the first section of the document.
Ask the four questions for that section and save the answer.
Paste the next section and ask the same four questions.
Ask: 'Combine your summaries into one, keeping the four questions and the quotes.'
Open the original and check two of the quotes against the document yourself.
advanced.hint: Section by section, then combine, then verify.
advanced.support: Break the big job into equal small jobs with the same questions each time. Combine only at the end, and finish with your own check.
advanced.explain: Pasting in sections keeps each answer within limits. The same four questions make the parts combinable, and checking quotes against the original is your guarantee.
